text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-severity: EU inference pool showing multiple nodes NotReady and kubelet restart loops. Customer 5xx spike detected. Paging on-call now.

sam_oncall: taking this. seeing 5xxs on text-gen routes and tail latency up. beginning triage.

lee_sre: looking at node fleet: infer-eu-05 and infer-eu-11 have repeated kubelet restarts (every ~30s). kubelet logs reference container runtime reconciliation failures.

tina_runtime: pulled model-worker logs from a restarted pod on infer-eu-11 — I see CUDA allocation failures immediately before process exit.

sam_oncall: paste the snippet please. need to know if this is app-level OOM or host GPU problem.

tina_runtime: ```
2026-03-16T09:42:01Z model-worker[pid=4512] WARN: Allocating 1.8GiB failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-16T09:42:02Z model-worker terminated: signal 9 (OOM?)
2026-03-16T09:42:03Z kubelet: Container runtime reported exit status 137
```

lee_sre: kubelet on infer-eu-05 also shows kernel messages around same time: `NVRM: Xid 79` and `GPU fell off bus`. That points to host-level GPU instability, not just process memory usage.

derek_runtime: routing telemetry: fallback to smaller model variants triggered at 09:44 UTC which lowered latency but 503s persisted until traffic drained away. Looks like pods kept crashing as they were scheduled onto affected hosts.

sam_oncall: immediate actions: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) drain them (ignore daemonsets), 3) scale up healthy eu replicas to absorb traffic, 4) shift a portion of traffic to us-west while we investigate. I'll cordon now.

sam_oncall: `kubectl cordon infer-eu-05 infer-eu-11 --context=prod-eu`

ops-rotation: standing by to assist with drains and to monitor eviction backpressure.

lee_sre: draining infer-eu-05 — eviction stalled due to large local cache volumes. using `--delete-local-data --force` to speed it.

deploy-bot: autoscaler adjusted: inference-deployment replicas eu 180 -> 240 to handle temporary load.

tina_runtime: while pods restart on other nodes, I'm flipping verbose allocator traces to capture exact allocation sizes. also lowering per-worker cache to 60% (WORKER_CACHE=0.6) on new pods.

lee_sre: infer-eu-11 drained and removed from service. kernel ring buffer shows repeated `nvidia-modeset: probe failed` entries before the Xid events.

maria_support: customers D and E reported 503s from 09:42 to 09:56 UTC. support notified and status page updated.

derek_runtime: added a temporary routing rule to prefer dedicated-capacity hosts with stable telemetry; disabled aggressive bin-packing autoscaler to avoid reassigning pods onto unstable hardware.

sam_oncall: opening INFRA ticket for GPU driver/firmware (INFRA-2027). tagging infra-team and attaching kernel traces.

incident-bot: Escalation: infra-team paged due to host GPU errors (Xid events).

eva_sre: taking over on-call in 20m. what's the current status?

sam_oncall: both flapping nodes cordoned and drained. no new NotReady nodes in the last 12m. error rate falling; traffic partly routed to us-west and dedicated pools. INFRA-2027 opened.

eva_sre: I will keep nodes cordoned. recommend not returning them until infra confirms driver/firmware health or hardware replaced.

tina_runtime: agreed. once infra gives the all-clear, we should redeploy with the original cache settings and run a gradual soak before full traffic restore.

lee_sre: also recommend a kernel driver upgrade on those hosts and temp blacklisting of the problematic GPU bus IDs until we confirm stability.

ops-rotation: monitoring dashboards — 95p latency and 5xx rate trending back to normal after routing adjustments.

maria_support: drafting customer-facing incident timeline and impact summary. will link to INFRA-2027 and include ETA for updates.

sam_oncall: marking incident as mitigated and handing off to eva_sre for monitoring and follow-up with infra. leaving channel open for root-cause work.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Handoff to eva_sre. Channel will remain open pending INFRA-2027 resolution.
